column2: cm_all_access at $6.99 produces greater-or-equal revenue per 1,000 paywall views than $4.99, because the 40% higher unit margin offsets a plausible conversion dip - the reasoning that raised the price from $4.99 in the first place (per the documented rationale: bounded downside + ladder coherence + the $7.26 ARPPU anchor; the Grand-shortlist revenue argument is immaterial at our scale)
column3: ofr_core with package all_access = cm_all_access at US $6.99 (locked launch default); RC Paywalls v2 copy unchanged
column4: Experiment-only offering ofr_core_b with package all_access = cm_all_access_499 at US $4.99; identical hero, headline, benefit list, disclosures and CTA text - only the price token differs, so the test isolates price
column5: post_level_5 (bonus_district shares ofr_core and is read as a secondary surface)
column6: Gross All Access revenue per 1,000 paywall_viewed at post_level_5 (report net at the 15% effective Play fee alongside; window revenue is the judged number)
column7: Relative conversion collapse >50% in the $6.99 arm; refund count via entitlement_changed(change=revoked); D1 retention of paywall viewers vs non-viewers
column9: At an expected 1.5-2% view-to-purchase, detecting a 1pp gap needs ~3.5k views/arm. Realistic in-window volume is low hundreds of views/arm, so this is DIRECTIONAL: decide on summed arm revenue, not on a p-value. Start Sep 1 at the latest so the read closes before the Sep 26-30 freeze
column10: Stop if either arm draws >=2 refund or complaint contacts; stop if both arms sit below 0.5% conversion after 500 views each (the problem is the paywall, not the price); stop immediately on any report of a player seeing both prices
column11: Medium - two live SKUs for identical content is a fairness optic. Mitigations: cm_all_access_499 is never advertised, never listed in ofr_shop, deactivated the day the test ends, and one install only ever resolves one arm
column12: RC Experiments (Pro/Enterprise-gated, verified 2026-07-31): server-side 50/50 on placement post_level_5, ofr_core vs ofr_core_b, no app update. FALLBACK if not on Pro: sequential offering change - repoint post_level_5 to ofr_core_b for 7d, back to ofr_core for 7d, split the readout by install week and disclose the day-of-week/news-cycle confound. Cross-ref experiment_backlog.csv E07-all-access-price (same test, run once, reported in both)

column2: Moving the first All Access exposure from the L5 win to the L8 win converts better, because deeper investment beats celebration context - if it does not, the locked L5 default is validated rather than assumed
column3: ofr_core carrying offering metadata {"first_exposure_level":5} - the client reads the metadata at boot and arms the post_level_5 moment on the first L5 win (locked default)
column4: Experiment-only offering ofr_core_t8: identical packages and identical paywall, metadata {"first_exposure_level":8} - the same placement, same creative, fired after the first L8 win
column7: D1/D3 retention; share of paywall_dismissed under 2s (annoyance proxy); total paywall_viewed volume must not collapse (an L8 gate reaches fewer players - report exposure rate alongside conversion)
column9: Two-layer problem: fewer players reach L8 than L5, so the variant arm fills slower AND converts on a smaller base. Expect low hundreds of views per arm - directional only. Report revenue per 1,000 INSTALLS as the tie-breaker, since conversion-per-view flatters the deeper gate
column10: Stop if fast-dismiss exceeds 70% of views in either arm, if D1 drops >3pp during the variant period, or if fewer than 30 variant-arm players reach L8 in the first 10 days (the arm cannot be read at all)
column11: Medium - revenue-touching and it moves the game's only system-initiated interrupt. The arm assignment must be sticky per install; a player must never see the paywall twice because the arm changed mid-life
column12: RC Experiments (Pro-gated, verified 2026-07-31) comparing ofr_core vs ofr_core_t8 - the timing lives in offering METADATA read at boot, which is what makes an otherwise client-side trigger server-testable. FALLBACK if not on Pro: sequential offering change - point post_level_5 at ofr_core_t8 for 7d then back for 7d and split by install week; metadata is edited in the dashboard either way, so no build is required. Cross-ref experiment_backlog.csv E06-paywall-first-exposure

column2: A content-led headline converts better than an interruption-free-led headline, because Cat Metro already ships with zero forced ads - so the fairness line reads as a promise to keep rather than a problem to solve, and it belongs at the bottom of the paywall, not the top
column3: ofr_core paywall (Paywalls v2): H1 "One ticket. Every line." with the five benefit rows first and the fairness/trust line last
column4: Experiment-only offering ofr_core_f with identical packages and price, paywall H1 "Yours forever. Never an interruption." - fairness line promoted above the benefit rows, everything else byte-identical
column7: Median paywall_dismissed view_duration_s; ANY review, support message or tester readback that interprets the copy as implying forced ads exist (this is a brand-promise guardrail, and it is absolute)
column9: Same math as PW01 - sub-1pp copy deltas are invisible at our n. Run it for direction and pair it with a comprehension question in the 12-tester script pre-launch. A null result still settles the internal copy debate and is a legitimate write-up outcome
column10: STOP IMMEDIATELY and revert to control if any tester or reviewer reads the variant as implying the game has forced ads; otherwise stop at 14 days and keep control on a null
column11: Medium - brand-promise adjacent. The whole positioning is 'fair by design'; copy that accidentally implies we removed a problem we never had would cost more than it converts
column12: RC Paywalls v2 variant swap. RC Experiments (Pro-gated, verified 2026-07-31) comparing ofr_core vs ofr_core_f, each with its own attached paywall. FALLBACK if not on Pro: sequential offering change / paywall edit - Paywalls v2 is remotely editable, so 7d + 7d requires no app update; split by install week and disclose the confound. Cross-ref experiment_backlog.csv E12-all-access-framing

column2: Promoting All Access from a one-line cross-sell to an equal third card in the theme sheet raises revenue per theme-preview view, because a player who wants one $2.99 theme is one step from the $6.99 edition that contains both - but it may cost theme sales and rental ad volume, which is exactly what the test measures
column3: ofr_themes packages ordered [theme_sakura, theme_neon, all_access] with all_access rendered as a single small cross-line under the two action rows (locked launch default)
column4: Experiment-only offering ofr_themes_b, same three packages, all_access promoted to an equal-weight third card directly beneath the two theme rows (still below them - never above the previewed item)
column6: Combined gross revenue per 1,000 paywall_viewed at theme_preview (theme purchases + All Access purchases attributed to this placement)
column7: cm_theme_sakura/cm_theme_neon purchase rate (cannibalization); rewarded theme_rental accept rate via ad_offer_viewed -> rewarded_ad_completed (a promoted upsell must not eat the ad row); preview -> any-action rate >=25%
column9: theme_preview is player-initiated, so volume tracks curiosity rather than sessions - expect a few hundred views per arm at best. Purchases will be single digits per arm; decide on summed revenue plus the rental-accept guardrail, not on rates
column10: Stop if theme purchase rate falls >40% relative in the variant, or if rental accept rate falls >25% relative (we would be trading ad revenue and a delight moment for an upsell that does not clear the gap)
column11: Low - cosmetic surface, player-initiated, no price changes. Main risk is the sheet becoming crowded enough that the live board preview (the actual selling mechanism) stops being the hero
column12: Pure offering-composition swap - the cleanest test in this set because only the package list and render role change. RC Experiments (Pro-gated, verified 2026-07-31) on placement theme_preview, ofr_themes vs ofr_themes_b. FALLBACK if not on Pro: sequential offering change - repoint theme_preview to ofr_themes_b for 7d then back for 7d, cohort-split by install week

column2: Anchoring the rewind sheet with the 20-pack first (and its true per-unit claim) raises rewind revenue per eligible-failure sheet view versus leading with the 5-pack, without increasing sheet dismissals - packs are a considered purchase, so the value anchor should be visible before the cheap option
column3: ofr_rewind packages ordered [rewind_5, rewind_20, all_access cross-line]; sheet renders the $1.99 5-pack first and the $4.99 20-pack second with the 'best per rewind' badge (locked launch default)
column4: Experiment-only offering ofr_rewind_b ordered [rewind_20, rewind_5, all_access cross-line]; the 20-pack leads with the same factual per-unit line ($0.25 vs $0.40) and the 5-pack follows. Free / owned / rewarded rows stay above both in every arm - that ordering is not testable
column6: Gross rewind-pack revenue per 1,000 paywall_viewed at rewind_failure
column7: Sheet dismissal rate and 'No thanks, retry from start' rate; rewarded rewind accept rate (rewarded_ad_completed per ad_offer_viewed); rewind_used(source=free) must remain the single most common source in both arms (fairness check); ledger reconciliation mismatches must stay at 0
column9: The sheet only opens on a player tap after attempt >= 2 with progress >= 40%, so eligible views accumulate slowly at launch scale - expect low hundreds per arm and single-digit pack purchases. Directional; pair with the 5-user think-aloud on the failure sheet
column10: Stop if dismissal rate rises >10pp in the variant, if rewarded accept rate falls >20% relative, or if free-source rewinds stop being the top source in either arm (that would mean the sheet had started selling instead of serving)
column11: Medium - this is the frustration moment. An anchor that reads as pressure would damage the one surface the whole 'never sell into frustration' principle is built around
column12: Offering-composition and ordering swap on ofr_rewind. RC Experiments (Pro-gated, verified 2026-07-31) on placement rewind_failure, ofr_rewind vs ofr_rewind_b. FALLBACK if not on Pro: sequential offering change - repoint rewind_failure to ofr_rewind_b for 7d then back for 7d, split by install week. column4: Experiment-only offering ofr_shop_b ordered [supporter, all_access, theme_sakura, theme_neon, rewind_5, rewind_20] - Supporter Pack as the top card with the Founder livery preview and the name-a-cat callout, still shop-only and still carrying the identical honesty line ('If you just want the content, All Access is the better buy.')
column6: Gross supporter revenue per 1,000 paywall_viewed at placement shop

column10: Stop if All Access shop conversion drops >30% relative, or on any refund of cm_supporter_pack with a reason indicating confusion about the overlap
column11: Low - shop-only surface that never interrupts, no price change, and the honesty line is present in both arms by construction

column2: RevenueCat Paywalls v2 renders crash-free at >=99.5% on the Android device matrix and converts at parity with the custom UGUI paywall; if either fails, the custom paywall ships at post_level_5 and Paywalls v2 is revisited after the event
column3: Custom UGUI paywall (the production renderer for the other four placements, therefore already hardened) rendering the identical section-4.1 layout on ofr_core
column4: RevenueCat Paywalls v2 via RevenueCatUI on the same ofr_core offering, same copy, same layout grammar
column6: Crash-free paywall render rate (renders without an armed-marker process death or an in-process RCUI exception); secondary: purchase_completed per paywall_viewed parity between renderers
column7: error_caught(domain=rcui_paywall) volume; paywall_viewed -> purchase_started funnel parity; zero cases where a strike-disabled device loses the ability to buy
column9: This is an engineering go/no-go, not a statistics exercise: 10 physical devices x 20 renders each pre-launch, then a 7-day live watch with a deterministic 50/50 client bucket (hash of the RC app user id). Devices that strike out of Paywalls v2 are force-migrated to custom - they still count in the reliability read but are excluded from the conversion read, and that exclusion is disclosed
column10: Any reproducible crash on a top-10 device, or any crash-free rate below 99.5% in the live watch, ends the test immediately and ships the custom renderer for the rest of the window; also stop if strike-disabled devices exceed 2% of the RCUI arm
column11: High if skipped - this is the purchase path on the highest-traffic commercial surface and there are three open Android paywall crash issues (#745/#736/#732) verified 2026-07-31
column12: Renderer choice is client-side, so RC Experiments cannot randomize it even on Pro - RC Experiments is Pro/Enterprise-gated (verified 2026-07-31) and would only be usable here if the arms were split into two offerings, which would confound the reliability read. Mechanism: deterministic client-side 50/50 bucket, with the same sequential-offering-change fallback discipline available (serve post_level_5 from an RCUI-attached offering for 7d, then a custom-rendered offering for 7d) if the client bucket has to be retired.
